name: DESI DR2 BAO measurements and cosmological constraints
notes: The abstract does not use the word "evidence"; the result type is measurement. The abstract adds: "Unless there is an unknown systematic error associated with one or more datasets, it is clear that ΛCDM is being challenged by the combination of DESI BAO with other measurements."

summary.plain: With three years of data and more than 14 million galaxies and quasars, DESI again found that standard ΛCDM fits well but is in mild tension with the CMB. A dark energy that changes with time fits better, preferred over ΛCDM at 3.1σ with the CMB and 2.8 to 4.2σ with supernovae.
summary.technical: BAO measurements from more than 14 million galaxies and quasars of DESI Data Release 2 (three years), combined with the Lyman-α forest BAO of a companion paper. Flat ΛCDM parameters are in 2.3σ tension with the CMB; the w0wa model (w0>-1, wa<0) is preferred over ΛCDM at 3.1σ for DESI BAO+CMB and 2.8–4.2σ when SNe are included. Σmν < 0.064 eV (ΛCDM) and < 0.16 eV (w0wa) at 95%.

title: DESI DR2 Results II: Measurements of Baryon Acoustic Oscillations and Cosmological Constraints
why_it_matters: The abstract states that, unless there is an unknown systematic error in one or more datasets, ΛCDM is being challenged by the combination of DESI BAO with other measurements; the results favour w0 > -1 and wa < 0, so a time-evolving dark energy.
